programs.name: RAMPAGE (3x/week full body)
programs.author: Geoffrey Verity Schofield
programs.summary: A three-day full-body hypertrophy program built around supersets of a press and a pull, with low set counts (2-3 per exercise) taken hard, often to failure plus partial reps. It is the example program from Schofield's ebook Resurrecting Your Gains, published free by him on Boostcamp.
programs.evidenceNote: Each muscle is hit about 3 times a week with roughly 6-9 hard sets per week for chest, quads and hamstrings at the minimum listed set counts and about twice that for back, which sits inside the range linked to good growth. Most sets are at RPE 8-10 or beyond failure with partials; lengthened-partial work has some supporting evidence but is still emerging, and frequent failure training raises fatigue. Several specialty lifts (Klokov press, Platz squat, Smith reverse-grip bench, Yates row) need equipment and mobility many gyms or lifters lack; the author lists swaps.

sources.title: RAMPAGE by Geoffrey Verity Schofield (Boostcamp, free program page, updated Oct 2026)
Resurrecting Your Gains: Finding Your Muscle Growth Formula (paid ebook the program comes from; not needed to run it)

programs.schedule: Full 1 on Monday, Full 2 on Wednesday, Full 3 on Friday; rest or optional low-intensity cardio on the off days. Exercises labelled as pairs are supersets (alternate the two).

progression.description: Author: aim for a double progression, adding reps until you reach the top of the rep range, then adding weight, and repeating. Not all sets need the same weight; you can do one heavier set then drop the weight if fatigue requires it. Sets are autoregulated (do the higher end of the 2-3 set range when you feel good, the lower end when life, tiredness or poor sleep show up; start on the lower side). Week 1 is easy to find working weights: the programming notes say ~3-4 RIR, the in-app week 1 note says ~6-7 RPE. From week 2, sets marked failure + partials go to failure, gradually adding partial reps in later weeks. Load increment is not specified by the author beyond 'adding weight'; the 2.5 kg values here are an app default, not from the source.
progression.deload: Built-in deload in week 5 and week 10: 'Just 1 set per exercise at the same intensity.' No other stall rule is stated.

programs.name: RAVAGE (6x/week Legs-Torso-Bro)
programs.author: Geoffrey Verity Schofield
programs.summary: A six-day Legs / Torso / Bro (arms and delts) split run twice a week, described by the author as a toned-down version of his own training. Sets are low (2-3) and taken very close to or beyond failure, with many press/pull and arm supersets.
programs.evidenceNote: Every muscle is trained twice a week with roughly 8-14 hard sets per muscle per week at the minimum listed set counts, including about 8 direct sets each for biceps, triceps and side delts from the two Bro days; that is consistent with hypertrophy evidence. Heavy use of RPE 9-10 and failure-plus-partials sets makes recovery the limiting factor, and the author explicitly says it is not for lifters without 1-2 years of solid training. Six sessions a week is a big time commitment for modest extra benefit over 4-5 well-built days.

sources.title: RAVAGE by Geoffrey Verity Schofield (Boostcamp, free program page, updated Oct 2026)

programs.schedule: Mon Legs 1, Tue Torso 1, Wed Bro Day 1, Thu Legs 2, Fri Torso 2, Sat Bro Day 2, Sun rest. Exercises labelled as pairs are supersets; the author prefers resting between the two movements to keep set quality.

progression.description: Author: use a double progression ('evolving rep range') whenever you can: when you get the top of the rep range on all sets, add the smallest amount of weight you can, which should reduce your reps, and repeat. Step loading (staying at a weight longer before jumping) can be used for small movements such as lateral raises, or progress range of motion on chest-supported rows. Sets: start at 2 per exercise and do the third when recovering well; 3-4 or 3-5 sets may suit lifters who respond to higher volume. Failure + partials: pick a weight you fail with a few reps short of the target, then add 2-3 partial reps. Increment is 'the smallest amount you can'; 2.5 kg here is an app default, not from the source.
progression.deload: Built-in deload in week 5 and week 10: 'Just 1 set per exercise at the same intensity.' No other stall rule is stated.

programs.name: Greg Nuckols Beginner Program (Strength)
programs.author: Greg Nuckols
programs.summary: A 12-week, 3-day beginner program that rotates four different full-body workouts, each with three main lifts and two accessories done as a descending-rep pyramid of three sets. This is the strength variation; the hypertrophy variation uses 5-8 / 8-12 / 12-15 on the main lifts, accessories are the same.
programs.evidenceNote: Stopping 1-2 reps short of failure on every set fits current evidence for beginners, and the pyramid gives both heavy and moderate-rep exposure. Because four workouts rotate over three days, each main lift is trained less than once a week and most muscles get roughly 4-9 hard sets weekly, which is on the low side for hypertrophy but fine for new lifters. No deload or stall rule is given.

Greg Nuckols Beginner Program - detailed program guide (Boostcamp)

programs.schedule: 3 non-consecutive days (Mon/Wed/Fri). Workouts A, B, C, D rotate continuously: week 1 A-B-C, week 2 D-A-B, week 3 C-D-A, and so on for 12 weeks.

progression.description: Program text: within each rep range, keep the same weight and aim for more reps each week until you have mastered it; e.g. in a 5-8 range, stay at the weight until you can do 9 reps, then go heavier but still able to do at least 5. In-app weekly note: start with last week's weights, aim for 1 more rep than before until you hit the top of the target range, then increase weight by 5-10 lb (about 2.5-5 kg here) and work back up within the range. Each set of the pyramid progresses on its own rep range.
progression.deload: No deload or stall rule is stated by the author.

programs.name: Novice Bodybuilding Program (Muscle & Strength Pyramid)
programs.author: Eric Helms, Andy Morgan, Andrea Valdez
programs.summary: A four-day upper/lower program with one strength-focused and one volume-focused session for each half of the body, all at about 2 reps in reserve on the first set. Weight goes up every week in fixed steps until the lifter stalls.
programs.evidenceNote: Each muscle is trained twice a week with roughly 9-12 sets per week for the big muscle groups at moderate proximity to failure, a sensible, recoverable novice dose. Direct arm work is light (2 sets per week each) and there is no direct side-delt work. Linear weekly load increases suit beginners but will stop working within months, at which point the authors say to switch to autoregulated double progression or the intermediate program.

sources.title: Novice Bodybuilding Program (RippedBody.com, Andy Morgan, updated 28 Dec 2025)
Novice Bodybuilding Program by Eric Helms (Boostcamp, official Muscle and Strength Pyramid account)

programs.schedule: Lower (Strength), Upper (Strength), Lower (Volume), Upper (Volume) once each per week, e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat. Spread them out and avoid more than two sessions back to back.

progression.description: Uses the authors' current version: RippedBody (updated 28 Dec 2025) gives first-set RIR 2 instead of %1RM or RPE and says to add a little weight each session while keeping form and the RIR target, then switch to autoregulated double progression once that stops working consistently. The Boostcamp version adds the exact steps: after the first session, if you hit the target reps, add 10 lb (~5 kg) to heavy lower-body compounds (squat, deadlift, hip thrust, leg press) and 5 lb (~2.5 kg) to everything else (bench, overhead press, rows, isolation work); if you miss, keep the weight. The first set is at about 2 RIR and the same weight is used for the remaining sets. %1RM (82.5% for 3x5 main lifts, 72.5% for 2x8 overhead press, 67.5% for 3x10 bench) is only a guide for the very first session.
progression.deload: Boostcamp/Pyramid rule: if you fail to hit your target reps in two consecutive workouts, reduce the load by 10%, then work back up. No scheduled deloads for novices.

programs.name: Intermediate Bodybuilding Program (Muscle & Strength Pyramid)
programs.author: Eric Helms, Andy Morgan, Andrea Valdez
programs.summary: A five-day Lower / Upper / Lower / Push / Pull program from the Muscle and Strength Pyramid authors, with compound lifts wave-loaded over 3-week waves and isolation work on double progression. Every fourth week is an optional deload decided by a short fatigue checklist.
programs.evidenceNote: Most muscles get about 10-16 sets per week across two sessions at roughly 2 RIR on the first set, squarely in the evidence-based range for intermediates. Wave loading gives built-in heavy-to-moderate variation and planned fatigue management. Weak points: direct side-delt work is absent (overhead presses and face pulls only), and the 4x3-5 squat and deadlift on the same day is demanding.

sources.title: Intermediate Bodybuilding Program (RippedBody.com, Andy Morgan, updated 28 Dec 2025)
Intermediate Bodybuilding Program by Eric Helms (Boostcamp, official Muscle and Strength Pyramid account)

programs.schedule: Lower, Upper, Lower, Push, Pull once each per week (Boostcamp: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat). Run the 4-week wave (3 loading weeks + optional deload) three times for 12 weeks, then repeat.

progression.description: Exercises and set/rep slots follow the authors' current RippedBody page (updated 28 Dec 2025), which uses first-set RIR 2 (=RPE 8, same weight for later sets) and says the program follows a wave-loading pattern but leaves the schedule to the book; the exact wave schedule below is from the official Boostcamp version. Compounds (3-5, 4-6, 6-8, 8-12 ranges): start at a weight where you can do all sets at the top of the range; each following week add load and drop one rep per set (two reps for 8-12 ranges). Boostcamp week notes say +10 lb (5 kg) for barbell squat and deadlift and +5 lb (2.5 kg) for everything else; the program description says +5 lb (2.5 kg) per week. After the deload the next wave restarts at the top of the range a little heavier than the previous wave's week 1. Isolation work in 12-15 ranges uses double progression: add reps each week toward 3 x 15, then add weight and restart at the bottom of the range.
progression.deload: Optional deload every 4th week: answer the checklist (dreading the gym? sleeping worse? loads/reps decreasing? more stress? more aches and pains?). Yes to 2 or more = deload: cut sets by about one third and use the lowest weight and reps from the previous 3 weeks. Yes to 0-1 = skip it and start the next wave.

programs.name: Built With Science #1 Full Body Workout Plan
programs.author: Jeremy Ethier (Built With Science)
programs.summary: Three different full-body workouts on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, each with five or six exercises for 3 sets, finishing with an isolation superset. It is the updated version of Jeremy Ethier's free full-body plan, published in full on his site with a companion video.
programs.evidenceNote: Each muscle is trained 2-3 times a week for roughly 6-9 sets per week for the major muscles (about 3 for delts and arms), enough for beginners and early intermediates but on the lower side for more trained lifters. Proximity to failure is not specified except that the last set of back exercises goes past failure with stretched-position partials. Progression is simple double progression with no deload or stall guidance.

sources.title: The #1 Full Body Workout Plan for Growth (FULLY EXPLAINED) - builtwithscience.com (modified May 2026)
The #1 Full Body Routine to Build Muscle & Lose Fat - Jeremy Ethier (YouTube)

programs.schedule: Workout 1 Monday, Workout 2 Wednesday, Workout 3 Friday. Pairs marked superset are alternated for 3 rounds.

progression.description: Author FAQ: add weight to the bar or dumbbells when you can complete all sets and reps with good form at the top of the recommended rep range (e.g. 12 clean reps on all sets of an 8-12 prescription), then increase the weight slightly next session; track weights and reps each session. Warm-up for the first lift: 1 light set of 8-10, then 3-5 reps heavier, then 1-2 reps heavy. The increment is only 'slightly'; 2.5 kg is an app default, not from the source.
progression.deload: No deload or stall rule is stated by the author.

days.name: Workout 1
days.focus: Upper chest, quads, mid back, hamstrings (knee flexion), arms

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.notes: Bench angle by sternum test (steeper sternum: 30-45 degrees). Elbows tucked in an arrow shape.

exercises.name: Barbell Squats
exercises.notes: Elevate heels on plates if you struggle to squat deep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Chest Supported Row
exercises.notes: 45-degree incline bench. Last set: after failure, 3-5 half reps in the stretched position.

exercises.name: Leg Curls
exercises.notes: Seated preferred, lying is fine. Don't fully straighten the knees between reps.

exercises.name: Lying Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.notes: Superset with overhead extension. Cable option: behind-the-body cable curl.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Overhead Extension
exercises.notes: Superset with the curl. Cable option: overhead rope extension.

days.name: Workout 2
days.focus: Chest strength, hamstrings (hip hinge), lats, glutes, side delts, abs

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: If heavy benching bothers your shoulders, go lighter for more reps or use flat dumbbell press.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Brace, push hips back, drive hips forward on the way up.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.notes: Fairly wide grip, lean back slightly. Last set: after failure, 3-5 half reps in the stretched position.

exercises.name: Glute-Focused Walking Lunges
exercises.notes: Reps per leg. Lean forward slightly for glute focus; back knee hovers above the floor.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Body Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.notes: Superset with reverse crunches. Cables 3-4 notches up from the bottom.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.notes: Superset with lateral raise. Knees to chest, curl the pelvis, control the way down.

days.name: Workout 3
days.focus: Front delts, lats, glutes, quads (rectus femoris), chest, calves, rear delts

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.notes: Bench 1-2 notches down from upright.

exercises.name: Lat-Focused Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Elbow tight to the side, sweep toward the hip. Last set: after failure, half reps in the stretched position.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.notes: Don't arch the lower back. Swap: dumbbell step-ups with a slight forward lean.

exercises.name: Leg Extensions
exercises.notes: Lean back if the machine allows.

exercises.name: Chest Flyes
exercises.notes: Seated cable fly preferred (pec deck alternative). Last set: half reps in the stretched position.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
exercises.notes: Superset with reverse cable flyes. Pause at the bottom for a deep stretch; legs straight.

exercises.name: Reverse Cable Flyes
exercises.notes: Superset with calf raises. Cables slightly above shoulder height, cross the cables.
